▶Data Management— clear-everything buttons, rarely needed
Use these to clear trial data after testing. They empty a whole table for everyone, straight away, and there is no undo and no backup. You have to type the word to confirm.
The audit log and every shipment record are never deleted by anything on this page. History stays.

Removes all ship box counts

▶Database setup (one-time)— only needed on a brand-new database
One-time setup — run both lines in your Supabase SQL editor. ship_segments lets a single SKU split across multiple shipments (8→FBA1, 2→FBA2) without merging. archived powers Archive Sent: archiving now hides rows from the prep sheet but keeps them on the Shipments page and in your stats. vat stores each product's VAT status (0% / 5% / 20%) for VAT-free flagging. The app works without these, but archived/split/VAT state won't survive a refresh until the columns exist. 
-- Every column this app writes, for every table it writes to.
-- Safe to run any time: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS never alters a column that
-- already exists, so this only ever fills gaps. Nothing is dropped or retyped.

-- Make sure every table exists before altering it. On a database that already
-- has them these are no-ops; they only matter on a fresh project.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prep_rows          (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS actions            (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lavarion_shipments (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lavarion_asins     (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS returns_skus       (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS returns_shipments  (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ship_boxes         (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log          (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid());

-- app_settings is key/value, so it is created rather than altered.
-- Postgres has no CREATE POLICY IF NOT EXISTS, so drop-then-create is the
-- idempotent form. Safe to re-run.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_settings (key text primary key, value text);
ALTER TABLE app_settings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "app_settings_all" ON app_settings;
CREATE POLICY "app_settings_all" ON app_settings FOR ALL USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);

⚠ This erases the shipment record
About to be deleted — permanently
What this does and does not do
• It only changes this app. It does not cancel or delete anything at Amazon — if the boxes physically went, they are still on their way.
• There is no undo. This is the only record of which shipment those units went out on, so once it is gone nobody can answer "where did those units go?".
• The units go back to being unsent, so they will look like they still need packing.
Only do this if
the row was marked sent by mistake and nothing actually left the building. If the stock really did go to Amazon, press Cancel — changing it here will not un-send it, it will just lose the record of it.
Not sure? Stop here.
Press Cancel, take a screenshot of this screen, and send it to Jack to look at. Nothing has changed yet and nothing will until you press the red button. Guessing on this one cannot be put right afterwards.
How many actually turned up?
In Warehouse means it is on the shelf and counted.
Nothing has been booked in against this row yet, so the count has to be entered before the status can say it arrived. Short? Put in what actually came — the rest stays outstanding.
Bulk Add Return SKUs
One SKU per line. Add a name after a space-dash-space if you want one — SKU - Logitech mouse — it is what UK staff see when prepping.
The name is optional. COG is read out of the SKU and every line comes in as 1 unit. Dashes inside a SKU are safe: only the first " - " splits the line.
